item.title: Texas engineers are building fish-like nano-robots that could harvest lithium from seawater and transform the future of clean energy
item.description: Texas A&M engineers are developing fish-like nano-robots to harvest lithium from seawater. These autonomous microscopic robots use specialised particles activated by light for movement. This innovative approach offers a sustainable alternative to traditional land-based mining methods.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: US Summer heat leaves multiple hikers dehydrated in New York's Adirondacks
item.description: New York Forest Rangers responded to a series of rescues across the Adirondacks in June, helping dehydrated hikers, treating medical emergencies, locating lost visitors and tackling a wildfire. Several incidents were linked to hot weather, prompting officials to remind people to carry enough water, prepare properly and follow hiking safety guidelines.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 34 killed as methane explosion tears through coal mine in Pakistan's Balochistan
item.description: A methane gas explosion in Pakistan's Balochistan province killed at least thirty-four miners. Ten miners remained trapped underground after the blast ripped through the coal mine. Rescue teams worked against time to locate and recover the remaining trapped workers. Authorities announced compensation for the families of the deceased miners. The incident highlights ongoing safety concerns within Pakistan's coal mining industry.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Mishra

item.title: German proverb of the day: "A fence lasts 3 years, a dog lasts 3 fences, a horse lasts 3 dogs, and a man lasts…"
item.description: An old German proverb highlights life's transient nature and the importance of valuing time. It uses symbolic lifespans to show everything has a limited existence. This message remains relevant as daily life continues to change rapidly. The proverb encourages appreciating ordinary moments and relationships over possessions. It reminds us that life's meaning comes from how years are spent, not just their length.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Tiny reef fish thrived near seabird islands; where rats wiped birds out, marine food chains changed
item.description: Tropical islands are facing a surprising ecological shift as invasive rats disrupt the balance of coral reef ecosystems. By decimating seabird numbers, these rats cut down on essential nutrient contributions to the reefs. As a result, tiny cryptobenthic fish flourish in nutrient-rich spots, while invertebrates find success in less fertile regions, reshaping the food web and highlighting the vulnerable nature of these priceless underwater habitats.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Spain migrant crisis: Military deployed as thousands cross border; 9 killed
item.description: Spain deployed its military to Ceuta after thousands of migrants crossed from Morocco. The sudden influx overwhelmed security forces, leading to a severe border crisis. Authorities confirmed an agreement with Morocco for the return of illegal migrants. The reason for the surge remains unclear, with various factors suggested. Ceuta, a Spanish enclave, is a key point for migration into Europe.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: 10 climbers, including Nirmal Purja, missing after avalanche on Broad Peak in PoK's Gilgit-Baltistan
item.description: Ten international climbers, including renowned Nepal-born mountaineer Nirmal Purja are missing after an avalanche struck Broad Peak. A tracking device shows Purja's location has shifted, offering a small hope for rescuers. Poor weather has so far prevented helicopters from taking off, delaying aerial search-and-rescue operations. Authorities were preparing to deploy helicopters on Friday morning if weather conditions improved.
item.dc:creator: Kanchan Yadav

item.title: Russian strikes across Ukraine kill 10; missiles hit Poland too
item.description: Russian missile and drone attacks killed at least ten civilians, including children, and injured over fifty. Nato scrambled warplanes after a Russian missile briefly crossed into Poland's western airspace. Ukrainian President Zelensky stated North Korean missiles were used in the attack on Thursday. Russia targeted Ukrainian air bases and arms factories, while Ukraine attacked Russia's oil sector.

item.title: xAI sues US state over law banning 'nudification' tech
item.description: Elon Musk's xAI company has sued Minnesota over its new law. This law bans AI nudification technology on websites and applications. The lawsuit challenges the state's authority to regulate AI-generated content. xAI argues the law is too broad and unconstitutional. The case could set a precedent for AI regulation by states.

item.title: Man hikes out of mountains to get help after getting impaled by a trekking pole
item.description: A nurse impaled himself on a trekking pole while climbing Montana's highest peak. He decided to self-rescue after assessing his condition and considering costs. The group carefully descended the mountain for over six hours. They reached a vehicle and drove to a clinic, then a hospital. Doctors removed the pole, and the nurse returned to work.

item.title: Why is DeenTheGreat reportedly facing up to 15 years in prison? Streamer’s lawyer makes fresh claim
item.description: Streamer DeenTheGreat, whose real name is Nurideen Shabazz, is facing felony robbery and misdemeanor battery charges linked to an alleged yacht incident in Miami. If convicted, he could face up to 15 years in prison. His lawyer says prosecutors are expected to dismiss the case soon, but the charges remain active ahead of his August 4 court hearing.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: Trump announces 'historic' Gaza deal as Board of Peace agrees on Hamas disarmament
item.description: Donald Trump announced a historic agreement for Hamas disarmament and Israeli withdrawal. This phased deal will establish a new Palestinian administration in Gaza. The Board of Peace facilitated this monumental step toward lasting peace and security. Mediators Egypt, Qatar, and Türkiye were thanked for their important efforts. Gaza will no longer pose a security threat after this significant progress.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Quote of the day by Pablo Picasso: "When I was as old as these children, I could draw like Raphael, but it took me a lifetime to learn to…"
item.description: Pablo Picasso admired children's uninhibited artistic expression and their natural imagination. He believed true mastery combined technical skill with this fearless approach. Older artists often lose this freedom due to fear of judgment and criticism. Picasso's journey shows simplicity achieved through experience is a higher achievement. Rediscovering this childlike curiosity is key to lifelong innovation and creativity.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Quote by Bertrand Russell: 'There are two motives for reading a book; one, that you enjoy it...'
item.description: Reading serves a dual purpose: it offers personal satisfaction while also catering to the desire for intellectual recognition among peers. This blend of motivations can drive individuals to choose books based on public perception rather than genuine interest. Psychological theories identify this as the contrast between intrinsic and extrinsic motivations. In our digital age, online platforms enhance this performative nature of reading.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Quote of the day by Leo Tolstoy: 'Everyone thinks of changing the world, but no one...'
item.description: According to Leo Tolstoy, true societal change begins with personal evolution. He asserted that individuals must first address their own imperfections. This mindset has significantly shaped leaders like Mahatma Gandhi and Martin Luther King Jr. However, in our contemporary society, there is a trend toward prioritizing external grievances over internal growth. To achieve meaningful advancements, it is essential to blend personal honesty with systemic change.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Before they were famous: “The moment you think you’ve made it, you stop growing”: How did Kai Cenat become one of the biggest streamers in the world?
item.description: Kai Cenat’s rise began with comedy videos on Instagram before expanding to YouTube, joining AMP, and later becoming one of Twitch’s biggest stars. His success came through years of consistent work rather than one viral moment. Today, his personality, audience connection, and creative live streams have made him one of the most influential digital creators in the world.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy
